review.rationale: The supplied Gold is a coherent independent expectation for this planning-only C bundle. The original PRD explicitly fixes OPT-1 as a hypothetical benchmark input, not a human Decision; ready with no blocking reasons is therefore appropriate for C, while a material unresolved DEC-001 must still block paired B at decisions. REQ-001, AC-001–AC-003, task keys, repository identity/base commit, writable binding scopes, and required evidence stages agree. The source evidence supports the selected scope: HTTPError owns message formatting, options.ts owns optional input and required normalized declarations, Ky.ts owns normalization and frozen snapshots, and constants.ts owns fetch-option filtering. Generic merge/forwarding and hook/type consumers appropriately remain inspection owners rather than mandatory edits. Build configuration supports generated distribution declarations rather than separately maintained declaration owners, and tsconfig.test.json includes the proposed test-d file. The implementation and independent verification split, verification dependency, and full required-AC coverage are specified. The allowed agents have matching roles, available capacity, and supplied active trusted claims for the relevant capabilities, including data.change and domain.state; the verifier additionally has testing.verification. Pending legacy claims and persona descriptions are not needed to establish eligibility. The configured independent reviewer satisfies the supplied non-executing review prerequisite. Gold and preview release fingerprints agree across repository, source, team, decisions, prompts, model, sampling, budgets, and metric policy. The distinct source-manifest/evaluation digest domains and PRD persistence normalization are explicitly explained by Service provenance. No candidates or historical candidate outputs are supplied, and isolation states Gold precedes every candidate on this bundle. This approval reviews the supplied evidence and mechanically bound fingerprints; it does not attest to human decisions, independently recompute digests, execute code, or establish test results.
